title: Compliance Onramp: Evidence Minimal Viable Set & Retention Matrix for Private/Dedicated Customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Define a Minimal Viable Set (MVS) of compliance evidence items and a retention matrix tailored for Private and Dedicated customers, with clear automation handoffs. This ticket produces: 1) an evidence MVS (what to collect for SOC2/ISO baseline during onboarding), 2) a retention matrix by artifact type (raw audit logs, parsed events, customer-facing artifacts, proofs), 3) the automation spec for evidence capture pipelines, and 4) a rollout plan and checklist for early enterprise pilots. Motivation: Customers onboarding to Private/Dedicated often ask for a narrow, auditable list of evidence we can generate automatically to reduce manual collection work and speed audits. Deliverables are intentionally conservative (MVS) to accelerate first audit cycles while leaving room to expand evidence scopes per customer requirements.
acceptance_criteria: MVS document published in Confluence with changelog and sign-off from Security and Legal
Retention matrix CSV uploaded to Drive and referenced from runbook
Automation spec includes event definitions, retention TTLs, and KMS/HSM handling for at-rest evidence
Pilot checklist with owner assignments and timeline, ready to run for 2 pilot customers
A lightweight dashboard in Grafana/Datadog showing evidence generation success rate >= 95% for pilot tests

2026-03-05 - Kickoff call notes: scoped MVS to 10 evidence items (login SAML traces, admin change events, audit log index, config snapshots, key rotation proofs) — agreed to revisit after stakeholder review
2026-03-09 - Security review (Marco Alvarez): requested stronger KMS mapping and explicit proof of destruction for transient debug archives; flagged legal review for retention beyond 3 years
2026-03-11 - Design input (Jelena Kovač): proposed retention UI for Console to let customers request extended retention per artifact; product-design to prototype by 2026-03-20

2026-03-12 - Engineering feasibility (Priya Rao): automatic collection feasible for SAML and auditlog ingestion; KV-cache config snapshots require lightweight agent for on-prem installs; estimated 5 engineering sprints for full automation; suggested phased approach: Phase A (automated collection + 90d retention defaults) then Phase B (custom retention policies + console controls)

2026-03-14 - Decision log: adopt phased approach. Phase A default TTLs: raw logs 90d, parsed events 365d, compliance proofs 7 years (hashed proofs and manifests only). Archival options via customer-requested exports. Approved by PM + Security.
2026-03-15 - Action items: 1) PM to publish Confluence draft; 2) ENG to open automation PRs and spike agents; 3) Legal to confirm 7-year proofs language; 4) Design to start Console prototype
risks: Under-collecting MVS causes auditors to request additional artifacts mid-audit (mitigation: include an escalation path and checklist for ad-hoc evidence collection)
Retention policy mismatch with customer legal obligations (mitigation: provide opt-in extensions and legal review step during onboarding)
On-prem agents may be blocked by customer network policies (mitigation: fall back to secure upload hooks and documented manual steps)
Too many artifact types increases engineering scope and delays pilot (mitigation: strict MVS and phased rollout)

notes: Trade-offs discussed: API-first evidence delivery vs agent-based collection. Chose phased approach to minimize customer friction and engineering risk.
Decided to store long-term proofs as hashed manifests with signer metadata to minimize PII risk while meeting auditor needs.
If pilot shows >10% manual evidence requests, we'll expand MVS and re-evaluate automation backlog.
